headline: Tax charges drive a loss; guidance cut, CEO to transition
summary_short: Revenue rose 3.3% y/y to $4,326M but Flutter swung to a $296M net loss (Q2 2025: $37M profit) after a $95M historical tax provision, cutting diluted EPS to -$1.57 from $0.59, and management lowered full-year 2026 guidance to $17.91bn revenue and $2.655bn adjusted EBITDA at the midpoint.
summary_long: Revenue grew 3.3% y/y to $4,326M (US -6%, International +10%, boosted by Snai/Betnacional), but Group adjusted EBITDA fell 44.7% to $508M on the UK gaming-tax increase, FIFA World Cup marketing spend and adverse US sports results. A $95M historical tax provision plus higher interest and D&A from M&A drove a $296M net loss versus $37M profit a year ago; diluted EPS fell to -$1.57 from $0.59. Free cash flow rose 21.2% to $189M; cash fell to $1,563M and long-term debt rose to $11,978M. Management lowered FY2026 guidance to $17.91bn revenue (from $18.305bn) and $2.655bn adjusted EBITDA (from $2.865bn) at the midpoint, and announced CEO Peter Jackson will hand over to Dan Taylor on October 1, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Release attributes growth to the Snai/Betnacional acquisitions, 'excellent FIFA World Cup engagement,' and International strength (SEA +36%), partly offset by a US sportsbook decline and an adverse y/y swing in US sports results.
Release cites the UK remote gaming duty increase (21% to 40%), FIFA World Cup marketing spend, and higher US promotional/technology costs from new-state launches and FanDuel Predicts investment.

Release attributes the swing to segment adjusted EBITDA declines, a $95M historical tax provision (India GST $62M, US Sales and Use Tax $33M), and higher interest expense and D&A from M&A financing, partly offset by a Fox Option fair-value gain.
Release ties the EPS decline directly to the net loss swing plus reduced non-controlling-interest benefits and lower income tax expense year-over-year.
Release attributes the related rise in interest expense to additional financing for the Snai and Betnacional acquisitions and the purchase of Boyd's 5% interest in FanDuel.

Release attributes the increase to a 1% rise in net cash from operating activities; free cash flow including financing capex and excluding player funds fell 56% on the same profitability and tax-timing factors.

CEO Peter Jackson will transition to Dan Taylor as CEO effective October 1, 2026 after nearly nine years leading Flutter; management also launched a new cost-transformation phase targeting $500m of gross savings by 2029.
